newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European Union rejects link to NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: European Union rejects link to NATO expansion.

text.p: The European Union official preparing the bloc's expansion to eastern Europe said on Tuesday that countries left out of NATO's own initial expansion could not count on EU membership as a consolation prize.

"They cannot expect us to help NATO out by automatically compensating any countries that should be excluded from NATO's first wave of enlargement. No automatic compensation," EU External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek said.

Addressing a seminar on the relation between the separate expansion plans of the 15-nation EU and the NATO military alliance, van den Broek said the European Commission would advise EU governments in July according to its own criteria.
NATO, at a summit set for July 8-9 in Madrid, is expected to itself invite number of eastern European hopefuls to the negotiating table, leaving others until later.
Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary are seen as favourites for NATO talks.

U.S. Ambassador to NATO Robert Hunter told the meeting that even though all might not be admitted at once, the door would remain open and warned those in the first wave against trying to veto entry by their eastern neighbours later.
"If they are going to veto someone else they may as well not apply," said Hunter.
He said that a country could only be admitted to NATO once it could play a full role in the alliance and be a provider as well as a consumer of security on the European continent.
